body:
I've tried setting default to '0' and value to '0' and it still goes to 1 ?

Is this because of the empty on https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/master/lib/Cake/View/Helper/FormHelper.php#L1410

Don't touch the value. You are confusing it with what it actually stands for (the integer representation of the boolean yes/no this field represents). Only modify the default value as outlined and documented.

I'm confused. I am trying to submit a checkbox with a zero value when checked? 

If I change the empty on:
https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/master/lib/Cake/View/Helper/FormHelper.php#L1410

To a !isset it works as I expect it.

Why would you want to give a checkbox a falsely value to post a checked checkbox? I figure a not checked checkbox then submits an empty string in your case?
In PHP it is usually quite dangerous as '' (nothing submitted), 0 and false are loosely coupled and easily confused/mixed.
That is why 0 stands for not checked, and 1 stands for checked.

So you should stick to the 0/1 defaults that the checkbox method provides or use a string based approach IMO.

EDIT: For edge cases like this (and with developers who know what they are doing) we could allow `isset()` in the FormHelper, though. Any objections?

@franksmule One think is the input value (what it represents) and another is whether is checked or not. Imagine this form:

What Do you prefer in your ice cream?:

[ X ] Bananas
[ ] Strawberries
[ X ] Chocolate

There are three checkboxes, with the values "Bananas", "Strawberries" and "Chocolate", and only two of them are checked. As you can see there are different attributes of the checkbox input element.

I'm closing this ticket as the bug's root cause is just a confusion of how html inputs work and we have enough documentation to explain how to work with this type of input.
@lorenzo I think he really wanted to modify the value that is posted :)
Gah, I came late to this discussion. Are you legitimately trying to set the value to '0'?

I want to legitimately set the value to 0. Examples of checkboxes that needs this:

Any negative wording for example - 'Don't add me to mailing list' - Some of the time it makes more sense to include the positive in database / programmatically, while displaying a inverted label to the user.

But as I mentioned before this is a dangerous game you are playing
Take a look at the test case: https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/blob/master/lib/Cake/Test/Case/View/Helper/FormHelperTest.php#L5638
It shows that the "not checked" value would usually be 0. What would you make that one then?

Why not just inverting it in the model layer upon save? Or using an "alias" field which then maps to the real one upon save. I would still not post falsely values as truthy ones.

I am currently inverting it in the controller its possible, but its just awkward. - Its much more intuitive in the view as to why its 0.

I understand why you need 0 to be the unchecked value, but its limiting an, in my opinion, important value. The best option for me is probably to extend the checkbox input to allow it.

I also feel its not made obvious in the documentation that 0 is an invalid value?

"0" is a valid value. just for the exact opposite - for the checkbox NOT to be checked. I can only refer to the linked test cases again. I don't think your case can be allowed without also modifying this "not checked" value, which really complicates things to a point where this is not justifiable.
It is also then really awkward as checked usually means Yes/1 and unchecked means No/0 - and in your case suddenly the opposite or alike. That is not intuitive and would probably confuse any developer working on that code in the future.

You can still use strings if you need some custom value passed, e.g. "not_published". Those can then be ported to the integer/boolean representation upon save as suggested earlier.

`'hiddenField' => '1'`
If someone forgets to set that second part it will probably fail to do what it is supposed to. Just as a side note.
Yep, but I don't think that FormHelper should magically swap one field depending on the other.

Yes, that's why I was against this change. But I guess, it is up to the developer to use it "properly" now :)
I wonder if it should be documented, though.

Woot! Thanks. This helped me solve a similar problem with a boolean value stored if someone has updated their password. In my CMS my language is 'Force this user to update password on login?', which means setting the value to 0.

Being able to do it in the helper takes away a task from my controller/model somewhere to swap them :smile:

i meet the same situation when i use the form component, one of my options's key is set to 0, it works fine when i post the data to the server, but the page can not get the right value, it returns the default value instead of zero.......
```php
echo $form->input('category', array(
    'label' => '标签',
    'type' => 'select',
    'options' => array(
        'all' => '全部',
        0 => '无',
        1 => 'abc',
        2 => 'def',
        3 => 'hij',
        4 => 'klm'
    ),
    'default' => 'all'
));
```
at last, i set the key to 'null', like this:
```php
echo $form->input('category', array(
    'label' => '标签',
    'type' => 'select',
    'options' => array(
        'all' => '全部',
        'null' => '无',
        1 => 'abc',
        2 => 'def',
        3 => 'hij',
        4 => 'klm'
    ),
    'default' => 'all'
));
```
it works fine.....
